title: feat(spec,plugin-auth): a short-lived principal-session mint, IAuthService.mintPrincipalSession, implemented by AuthManager
body:
Fixes #23772

Clause-②: yes

## What this does

S2 of #22269: a short-lived session for the requesting user's OWN principal, so an in-process service (the print service's headless browser, local or remote) can load a page as that user, never as a system principal (#8346 ruling B′, M2).

- **`@objectstack/spec`** (`contracts/auth-service.ts`): one optional `IAuthService` member, `mintPrincipalSession(context, options?)`, its types (`PrincipalSession`, `PrincipalSessionCookie`, `PrincipalSessionMintOptions`), and `PRINCIPAL_SESSION_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 120`. The `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` shards are regenerated: 4 exports added, 0 removed.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-auth`**: `AuthManager.mintPrincipalSession`, which delegates to the new `principal-session-mint.ts`. That module owns the refusals, the TTL, the non-extension guard and the revoke. `composeDatabaseHooks` gains one `session.update.before` hook. A host hook runs first and its `false` is honoured.
- No HTTP route. The impersonation paths are untouched.

## The mechanism, measured against better-auth 1.7.3 (`node_modules`, not the range)

| Zone 2 hypothesis | Verdict |
|:--|:--|
| 1. Only two `internalAdapter.createSession` callers | **Holds, re-measured.** `admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts:325` (it was `:228`) and `impersonation-bearer-rotation.ts:251`. Both were read for the shape. The mint calls `createSession(userId, false, { token, expiresAt, activeOrganizationId }, true)`. `overrideAll` is required because `createSession` writes `expiresAt` after the override spread (`dist/db/internal-adapter.mjs:261-277`). Neither impersonation path is used. `impersonatedBy` stays unset. |
| 2. The refresh trap, on both lanes | **Holds, and the bearer lane is worse than the card said.** `get-session` renews when `expiresAt - expiresIn + updateAge` is in the past (`dist/api/routes/session.mjs:180`), and a 120 s session meets that on its first read. It then writes `now + expiresIn` (`:200`). Only a signed dont-remember cookie or `disableRefresh` skips this (`:170`). `bearer()` rewrites only the session-token cookie (`dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs:46`), and the in-process bearer read renews by design (`inProcessSessionReadInput`). So a client-side defence covers the cookie lane only. **The defence is server-side, on the one write every renewal makes**: `internalAdapter.updateSession` runs `session.update.before` before it writes, under secondary storage too (`dist/db/with-hooks.mjs:43-60`). `holdPrincipalSessionExpiry` pins a minted session's `expiresAt` to its stored value. A minted session is identified by its token prefix `psm_`, which the server sets and stores on the row. The non-extension is pinned on each lane: cookie over HTTP, bearer over HTTP, and the in-process bearer read. |
| 3. TTL short, fixed maximum | **120 s, a ceiling the caller cannot raise.** A larger `ttlSeconds` is **refused** (`VALIDATION_ERROR` / `400`), not clamped (axis 3: a loud contract over silent tolerance). 120 s is the design report's number: a local render measured about 1.3 s (launch 954 ms, render 341 ms), and the rest is slack for the remote placement and page load. |
| 4. Revoke reads as no session on both lanes | **Holds.** `revoke()` is `deleteSession`, bound to the one token and idempotent. Afterwards both HTTP lanes answer `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, the platform's ruled no-session answer (`anonymous-session-refusal.ts`). The in-process read answers `null`, and the row is gone. |
| 5. Refusals before any mint; the predicate reused | **Holds.** No `ExecutionContext`-level "is human" predicate exists. `git grep` finds only `isGuestPrincipal` (plugin-security and plugin-sharing) and `isPerfDisclosurePrincipal`. The judgement is therefore the spec's own declaration: `principalKind` absent means `human`, plus `isSystem`. On the row it reuses `isHumanUserRow` (the predicate the audience gate and dev seed read). On posture it reuses `judgeHeldSession`, the same judge the impersonation endpoint uses, over the carried `authGate` **and** a live `resolveUserAuthGates`. An API key is not told apart: ADR-0090 D10 rules a key a credential of its owner, so its context is the owner's human principal (see the open questions). |
| 6. Cookie names honour `cookiePrefix` / `__Secure-` | **Holds.** Name and attributes are `authContext.authCookies.sessionToken`, better-auth's derivation from the `advanced.cookiePrefix` / `useSecureCookies` that `AuthManager` passes (`auth-manager.ts` `advanced` block). Nothing is restated. Pinned: `better-auth.session_token` on http; `__Secure-acme.session_token` (secure) under prefix `acme`, and that cookie authenticates. |
| 7. Clause-② on two surfaces; existing implementers compile | **Holds.** No class in `packages/` declares `implements IAuthService`. The 8 files that name the type are readers (`IAuthService \| undefined`) or the slot map (`core-service-contracts.ts`), and an optional member changes nothing for them. A compile-time pin assigns `AuthManager.mintPrincipalSession` to the contract's own member type (`IAuthService` with every member required, indexed at `mintPrincipalSession`), so the two cannot drift. |

Refusal order, all thrown as `PrincipalSessionMintRefusalError` (`code` + `status`) before `createSession` is reached:

1. No user, `isSystem`, or a non-`human` `principalKind`: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403`.
2. `ttlSeconds` outside 1..120, or not an integer: `VALIDATION_ERROR` / `400`.
3. A carried `authGate`: `403`, with the posture code.
4. User row missing, not human, or banned with no lapse: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403`.
5. A live posture: `403`, with the posture code.

## Pins

- `principal-session-mint.cookie-lane.pin.test.ts`: a control (an unbranded 120 s session IS renewed by the same read); the minted cookie authenticates and its expiry does not move over 3 reads, in the row and in the answer; revoke.
- `principal-session-mint.bearer-lane.pin.test.ts`: a control; HTTP bearer over 3 reads; the in-process bearer read; revoke on both.
- `principal-session-mint.test.ts`: every refusal asserts `code` + `status`, that `createSession` was never called, and that no `sys_session` row appeared. Also: TTL default and a shorter ask, the active organization, the brand, the cookie on http, the prefixed `__Secure-` cookie, the guard function itself, and the contract-assignability pin.
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.test.ts`: the member stays optional; the ceiling is 120.

**Ablation** (one-shot, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on the committed fix). `const held = holdPrincipalSessionExpiry(draft, ctx);` was replaced with `const held: any = undefined;`. The anchor went 1 to 0, blob `00e04f1c266a` to `eb8c5dc5e4fc`. The tests import the module from `src` (relative), so no dist is involved. Result: **3 failed / 24 passed**. All three non-extension pins went red (cookie, bearer HTTP, bearer in-process); the controls and revokes stayed green. Restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD `00e04f1c266a` and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Tests and gates

All readings are on this branch. Code and tests were measured at `e3db58a8`, and the final head `53e173d2` adds one docs row on top.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (whole package): **149 files, 2921 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**.
- The three mint files alone: 60/60, then 61/61 after the contract-assignability pin.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0. That covers `tsc` on src, the examples config, and `check:test-typecheck` (OK; the debt is unchanged at 10 files / 88 errors / 23 pinned signatures, and the new tests add none).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/auth-service.test.ts`: 9/9. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build && … check:generated`, re-run after merging `origin/main`: all 14 artifacts are up to date. Before that, `--fix` regenerated only the two shards it proved stale.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on the final head: 111 families. `--ran` reconciliation: **111 derived, 107 run, 4 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun**. Every one of the 107 that ran exited 0.
  - `node scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs` first exited 1 with a real finding: the mint's system-context refusal had no row on `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`. Row 61b was added and the census now passes. That docs page is outside the claimed file surface; the gate requires it.
  - NOT MEASURED, exit 3 (the gate refused its own prerequisite): `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` (its fixture commit is outside this shallow clone), `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (41 workspace packages have no local dist), and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` (another package's declarations are absent). CI runs all three.
  - NOT MEASURED, exit 124: `pnpm check:type-check-debt` hit a 300 s local timeout before the whole-workspace ratchet reached a verdict. CI runs it.
- Local-only `pnpm check:dev-prereqs`: exit 1, because 2 unrelated packages (`cli`, `organizations`) have no local dist. It does not flag spec, and it is not a reading of this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- A minted session fires the existing `session.create.after` audit writer, so each mint leaves a `login` row for the user with no endpoint in its context. This is an observation; the consumer card may want to say whether a render should be audited differently.
- While a minted session lives (at most 120 s), ADR-0069 D4's concurrent-session cap sweep counts it if the user signs in elsewhere in that window. This is an observation.
- The line `[AuthManager] better-auth returned error: 500 {"message":"Failed to find admin session"}` appears once per fixture boot in these suites and 14 times across the existing plugin-auth suite. It predates this PR.
- Line budget: +963 / -2 (965) against the card's estimate of about 560–640. The excess is test and module prose: three pin files plus a shared fixture (about 480 lines), and a module header that states each measured trap.
